title: Burst entropy synchronizer and spectral sample encoder
author: Samir Patel
commits: Initial spike: add burst entropy synchronizer core and scheduler hooks
Add spectral sample encoder Python implementation and unit tests
Integrate benchctl CLI command and report serializer
CI: pipeline for end-to-end profile with compressed export
Address review comments: concurrency guards and deterministic seed handling
description:
Summary: Introduce a microtemporal "entropy" synchronizer that detects and coalesces short-lived burst events across worker threads and a complementary spectral sample encoder that compresses sampled telemetry for long-term fidelity analysis. Motivation: our existing burst detectors miss correlated microbursts that span CPU/GPU kernel boundaries; this patch implements cross-stream correlation and a compact export format to retain enough signal for offline spectral analysis without exploding storage.

What changed (design + behavior):
- benchlab/samplers/burst_entropy_sync.cc: new lightweight synchronizer that collects sub-10ms burst markers, aligns them using monotonic timestamps, computes per-kernel entropy metrics and emits aligned events to the reporting queue. Built to be non-blocking and tolerant of clock skew between processes.
- benchlab/encoders/spectral_sample_encoder.py: spectral encoder that converts event streams to a compressed spectral slice (.ssf) format using a small DCT-based projection + run-length packing. Designed for downstream spectral heatmap generation and correlation with KV-cache pressure traces.
- benchlab/tools/benchctl/commands.py: new CLI command `benchctl export-spectral` to generate compressed exports from a run; supports streaming to S3/local and configurable retention window.
- benchlab/reports/compressed_fidelity_format.md: spec for the .ssf export, fields, and suggested decoder algorithms for offline analysis.
- benchlab/tests/test_entropy_sync.py: unit and deterministic fuzz-style tests; added seeding harness to make bursts deterministic in CI.
- benchlab/ci/bench_profile_pipeline.yaml: CI job that runs a short synthetic workload to validate synchronizer + encoder and asserts size and latency regressions.

Performance notes: In a synthetic multi-kernel workload (3 concurrent kernels with artificially injected sub-15ms bursts), the synchronizer identified 98% of correlated bursts vs 63% for the previous thresholded detector. End-to-end export overhead measured at ~1.8% CPU and <2ms p95 added latency in a profiling run (defaults are conservative). Compressed .ssf output reduced raw event payloads by ~8x on our sample runs.

Testing and CI: The bench_profile CI job runs the deterministic workload locally and then validates that produced .ssf files decode and contain expected spectral peaks. One transient flaky assertion occurred on the first run due to a race in the test harness; fixed by adding an explicit flush and retry in tests. All CI checks green on final push.

Review conversation (high level):
- Priya: requested that the synchronizer avoid allocation in the hot path; addressed by switching to a fixed slab allocator and reusing event buffers.
- Diego: asked for stronger determinism in tests; I added seeded timers and a replay harness to guarantee event placement.
- Ava: questioned the compression format and backward compatibility; added a short format spec and provided a compatibility shim for the old JSON-based exports.
The comments thread closed after two follow-up commits that tightened concurrency guards and improved test coverage.

Backward compatibility and migration: The new .ssf export is opt-in; benchctl continues to produce the previous JSON exports. The report spec documents a migration path and a small Python shim (in encoders/) to decode .ssf into legacy JSON for downstream tooling during rollout.

Related tickets: ENG-4821 (multi-kernel microburst detection), ENG-4890 (compressed profile exports for long-term storage).

Release notes: (internal) Add a new microburst alignment sampler and compressed spectral export to benchlab. Opt-in export via `benchctl export-spectral`. Expected to reduce profiling storage by ~8x for burst-heavy workloads and improve correlated-burst detection accuracy.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
